default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-378.title: Gap-in break bar fade
E-378.hypothesis: A short-term break that was printed by the bar's opening jump (the bar opened beyond the level, above the previous close) and then traded back against it inside the bar was made by a quote vacuum at the bar's open, not by buyers lifting offers: the buyers who chased the open are already under water within the bar and liquidity providers keep leaning on the gap, so fade the break (mirror for down-breaks).

E-379.title: Neutral-day micro-break fade
E-379.hypothesis: Market Profile's neutral day: once the session has extended both above and below its initial balance, both the other-timeframe buyers and sellers have tried and been answered, so the day is traded responsively from both edges; a short-term break inside such a two-sided session has no initiator behind it and is faded (extension on BOTH sides, unlike the unextended or wide-IB interiors already screened).

E-380.title: Developing-POC stretch fade
E-380.hypothesis: Today's developing point of control is the price where most of today's contracts changed hands, i.e. the price both sides currently accept; after the first hour a move several typical half-hour moves away from it is carried by a thin crowd, and the first bar closing back beyond the previous bar's extreme starts the return toward the accepted price as responsive traders lean in (a stretch from today's POC, not VWAP or yesterday's POC).

E-381.title: Repeated-break fatigue fade
E-381.hypothesis: When the same side has already broken short-term highs several times within the last hour, each new break is bought mostly by late chasers while the early breakout buyers are taking profit into it and the stop pool above has been cleared repeatedly; the m-th same-side break inside an hour is therefore exhausted flow, so fade it on the break bar itself (mirror for lows).

E-382.title: Larry Williams setup 9.3 trigger
E-382.hypothesis: Setup 9.3 (rising 9 EMA, two closes below a reference close, buy on the break of the last bar's high) is taught alongside 9.1/9.2 to Brazilian WIN day traders; the two-bar pullback traps short-term sellers whose stops sit just above, and the setup users' buy-stops at the same place fill together, so follow the trigger (mirror on a falling EMA).

E-383.title: Raschke 80-20 reversal
E-383.hypothesis: Raschke/Connors' 80-20: a large bar that opened in its top fifth and closed in its bottom fifth draws momentum sellers at its close; when the next bar trades below that bar's low and closes back above it, the sell-stops under the low have been run and found no follow-through, the late sellers are trapped, so buy the reclaim (mirror for a bar that opened low and closed high).

E-384.title: Turtle Soup Plus One
E-384.hypothesis: Raschke's Turtle Soup Plus One on intraday bars: a close below a window low that was made at least four bars earlier triggers the breakout sellers and the stops of the old low's buyers; if the very next bar closes back above that old low, the break is a failed liquidity raid and the trapped breakout sellers cover, so buy the reclaim (mirror for highs); the one-bar wait and the old-level condition differ from fading the break bar itself.

E-385.title: Two-day value conflict micro-break fade
E-385.hypothesis: When price sits between today's session VWAP and yesterday's full-session VWAP while the two are clearly apart, the holders of today's inventory and of yesterday's inventory are on opposite sides of their cost and defend opposite edges; neither camp follows a short-term break inside that band and the other absorbs it, so fade breaks in the conflicted zone.

E-386.title: Hourly Crabel stretch break follow
E-386.hypothesis: Crabel's stretch (the average of the smaller of open-to-high and open-to-low) measures how far price normally wanders against the eventual direction from an open; applied to each clock hour with the same hour of the previous sessions, a first close beyond hour-open +/- m stretches means this hour has gone further than noise usually takes it, so a parent order is working that way; follow the first such close in the hour.

E-387.title: Same-half-hour return seasonality follow
E-387.hypothesis: Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka find returns persist at lags that are exact multiples of a trading day: the same half-hour keeps its sign across sessions because institutions rebalance and execute on fixed daily schedules; at the last bar before each half-hour, when that coming half-hour's mean return over the previous sessions is large relative to its dispersion, trade in its sign.
